reason: $id_dependente is checked with is_numeric() and the request is rejected with 400 before the query, so only numeric values can reach the interpolated SQL, which is not injectable.
$almox comes straight from $_REQUEST and is concatenated into the mysqli query with no validation, casting, or parameterization, which is a classic SQL injection.
This is the minified public @docsearch/js library bundle with no credentials or secrets of any kind, so CWE-798 (hardcoded credentials) does not apply.
The embedded keypairs live in a tlstest helper package explicitly meant only for tests (CN alt.test/localhost), a standard test-fixture pattern, not production credentials.

The shell() helper in create-astro is invoked with developer-controlled commands and flags from the CLI scaffolder itself, not attacker-controlled input, so shell:true here is a style concern rather than an exploitable command injection.

The value is constrained by preg_match('/^[a-z0-9]*$/') and used only to include a local .php file under a fixed directory with is_file check, so no URL/request is made and CWE-918 (SSRF) is inapplicable.
load() evals the application's own local config file (not user input) and executes no OS command at all, so CWE-78 command injection does not apply to this code.
unserialize() of $_POST['config'] is mitigated: PHP7+ path passes allowed_classes=false and the legacy path rewrites object tokens into __PHP_Incomplete_Class, blocking object injection gadgets.

The ${{ inputs.* }} values come from a workflow_call of a reusable workflow (typed boolean/string supplied by trusted caller workflows in the repo), not from untrusted PR-controlled context, so there is no realistic command injection.
In the shown code $version/$revision are only compared against whitelists via array_key_exists/version checks and never concatenated into any SQL statement, so no CWE-89 injection is evident.
